detailed_section_hierarchy.section_number_title: 10.1 Characteristics of Sound Waves and Echoes
detailed_section_hierarchy.full_explanation: Sound requires a medium (solid, liquid, gas). Speed of sound v = frequency * wavelength. Reflection obeys laws of reflection; echoes require minimum 17.2m distance.

glossary_and_key_terms.definition: Region in a longitudinal wave where medium particles are crowded together under high density and pressure.

formulas_rules_and_laws.name: Wave Equation
formulas_rules_and_laws.model_application_example: f = 256 Hz, lambda = 1.3 m -> v = 332.8 m/s.

formulas_rules_and_laws.name: Echo Distance Formula
formulas_rules_and_laws.variable_definitions: d=distance to reflector (m), v=speed of sound, t=echo time (s)
formulas_rules_and_laws.model_application_example: Echo heard after 0.2 s at 344 m/s -> d = (344*0.2)/2 = 34.4 m.

m3_practical_activities_lab_and_step_by_.activity_or_procedure_title: Verifying Laws of Reflection of Sound Waves
m3_practical_activities_lab_and_step_by_.objective_or_aim: Demonstrate equal incident and reflected sound angles.
step_by_step_procedure: Position pipes at angle to wooden board.
Place ticking clock at end of Pipe 1.
Adjust angle of Pipe 2 until ticking sound is maximum.
Measure incident angle i and reflected angle r.
m3_practical_activities_lab_and_step_by_.expected_observations_or_working: Maximum loudness occurs when angle of incidence equals angle of reflection.
m3_practical_activities_lab_and_step_by_.scientific_or_logical_conclusion: Sound waves reflect obeying equal-angle reflection law.
